sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE G. S. AHLUWALIA

ON THE 7 th OF AUGUST, 2025  SECOND APPEAL No. 131 of 2011  IRSHAD KHAN AND OTHERS  Versus  HAMEED KHAN AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Mr. Prashant Sharma - Advocate for appellants.
 Mr. C.R. Roman - Advocate for respondent No. 1.
 Mr. Shohit Mishra - Govt. Advocate for respondent No.
 JUDGMENT

This second appeal under Section 100 of CPC has been filed against judgment and decree dated 21.10.2010 passed by District Judge, Vidisha in Regular Civil Appeal No. 24-A/2009, as well as judgment and decree dated 26.06.2009 passed by Civil Judge, Class I, Kurwai, District Vidisha in Civil Suit No. 37A/2008.

entities.text: Civil Judge, Class I, Kurwai, District Vidisha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The Appellants are the plaintiffs who have lost their case from both the Courts below.

3. The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that agricultural land bearing Khasra Nos. 202/2, 219, 220/1, 240/1, 263, 264/1, 264/2, 267, 270, 272, 414, 416/1, total area 7.961 hectares, situated in Village - Suneti is the disputed property.
It is the case of plaintiffs that Daraj Khan, S/o Raje Khan, was the owner of the disputed property who expired NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18277 2 SA-131-2011 on 13.09.2004.
According to plaintiffs, Daraj Khan had three sons, namely, Ameer Khan, Habeeb Khan, and Hameed Khan, whereas he had one daughter Hallo Bi.
Wife of Daraj Khan, namely, Ganni Bi, son Habeeb Khan, and daughter Hallo Bi had died during the lifetime of Daraj Khan.

It was further pleaded that two years prior to the death of Daraj Khan, his another son Ameer Khan had gone to Bhopal to meet his sons Arif and Tarikh, but while coming back, he went missing and his whereabouts are still not known.

Plaintiffs Nos. 1 to 3 are the sons of Habeeb Khan, and plaintiffs Nos. 4 to 6 are the sons of Ameer Khan, whereas defendant No.
1 is Hameed Khan.

It was claimed by plaintiffs that on account of death of Habeeb Khan, and Irshad Khan vs Hameed Khan on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126757293/
1 missing of another son of Daraj Khan, namely, Ameer Khan, Late Daraj Khan was very sad, and he was also very old, and accordingly, plaintiffs, as well as defendant No. 1, were jointly looking after the land belonging to Daraj Khan and were maintaining the entire family.
It was pleaded that Daraj Khan, about one and a half years prior to his death, partitioned the property in three shares.
1/3rd share was given to plaintiffs Nos. 1 to 3, 1/3rd share was given to plaintiffs Nos. 4 to 6, and 1/3rd share was given to defendant No. 1, and accordingly, verbal Hiba was also announced.

Verbal Hiba was graciously accepted by plaintiffs and defendant No. 1, and accordingly, possession of the same was also handed over to the respective parties, and thus, it was pleaded that all the respective parties are in possession of the land which was given to them by verbal Hiba, and they are looking after their families.

It is submitted that plaintiffs Nos. 1 to 3, plaintiffs Nos. 4 to 6, as well as defendant No. 1 have equal share in the property in dispute, but NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:18277 3 SA-131-2011 taking advantage of the precarious condition of plaintiffs

,
defendant No. 1 prepared a forged Will of Daraj Khan, and on the basis of said forged Will, got his name mutated in the revenue records.
Plaintiff No. 4 had also filed an appeal against the order of mutation, but the same was dismissed by the S.D.O.
It was also claimed that defendant No. 1 was openly saying in the village that he would subsequently partition the land in three parts because, at present other co-sharers will spoil the property.

When plaintiffs requested defendant No. 1 to get their names mutated in the revenue record, then defendant No. 1 clearly denied the title of plaintiffs,
and accordingly, it was pleaded that denial of title by defendant No. 1 has compelled the plaintiffs to file a suit for declaration of title.
4. Defendant No. 1 filed his written statement and claimed that Daraj Khan did not expire on 13.09.2004, but he died on 14.03.2004.

It is not out of place to mention here that the written statement, which was filed by defendant No. 1, was in a very sarcastic manner, and lot of questions were raised by defendant No. 1 with regard to honesty and correctness of pleadings made by plaintiffs.
In nutshell, it was claimed by defendant No. 1 that he is the only surviving son of deceased Daraj Khan, and therefore, he is the owner and in possession of the land in dispute.
5. The Trial Court, after framing issues and recording evidence, dismissed the suit.
6. Being aggrieved by judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, appellants/plaintiffs preferred an appeal, which too has been dismissed by the Appellate Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18277 4 SA-131-2011 7.

Challenging the judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that there is nothing in the Muslim law to show that only surviving son would inherit the property, and legal representatives of pre-deceased sons would not get any right, and accordingly,
appellants have proposed the following substantial questions of law:-

"(i) Whether the learned Courts below have erred in law in dismissing the suit holdin that the appellants have no right to succeed to the property?
Irshad Khan vs Hameed Khan on 7 August, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126757293/
2
(ii) Whether the finding recorded with regard to succession in Muslim Law is on wrong judicial notions whereby the predeceased sons' heir has been disinherited?

(iii) Whether the judgment being passed in ignorance to the provisions of chapter VI of Muslim Law is not sustainable particularly when the appellants fall within the category of sharer in the property of the grandfather?"

8. Heard learned counsel for appellants.
9.
Plaintiffs, who claim themselves to be the sons of Habeeb Khan and Ameer Khan, have not filed the suit on the basis of inheritance, but they have filed the suit on the basis of Hiba.
No arguments have been advanced by counsel for appellants on the question of Hiba.
10. Both the Courts below have given a concurrent finding of fact that appellants have failed to prove that any oral Hiba was done by Daraj Khan.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18277 5 SA-131-2011 The Appellate Court has considered the discrepancies in the evidence of witnesses with regard to Hiba.

11. Irfan Khan (PW-2) has stated in paragraph 6 of his examination- in-chief that about one and half years prior to death of Daraj Khan, he had declared open Hiba in favour of plaintiffs and defendant No.1.
However, in paragraph 10 of his cross-examination, he has stated that Daraj Khan had declared open verbal Hiba about 10-12 years prior to his death, and Hiba was also written.

It was stated that the signatures of beneficiaries were obtained on the partition, whereas Sakir Khan (PW-1) has stated that verbal Hiba was done by Daraj Khan about two years prior to his death, and it was specifically stated that Hiba was not a written one.
12. Ayub Khan (PW-3) has stated that Daraj Khan had done oral Hiba about 3 to 4 years prior to his death.
He has also admitted that earlier he was tried for an offence under Section 376 of IPC.
13. Thus, there is a discrepancy in the evidence of the witnesses as to when oral Hiba was done by Daraj Khan.

14. Accordingly, this Court is of considered opinion that both the Courts below did not commit any mistake by giving a concurrent finding of fact that plaintiffs have failed to prove that any oral Hiba was done by Late Daraj Khan.
15. In the present appeal, appellants/plaintiffs have proposed the substantial questions of law with regard to inheritance.
16. The Appellate Court has given a finding of fact that plaintiffs have failed to prove that Ameer Khan has died a civil death.

Under these NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18277 6 SA-131-2011 circumstances, as the appellants have failed to prove that Ameer Khan has died a civil death as his whereabouts were not known for the last seven years, this Court is of considered Irshad Khan vs Hameed Khan on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126757293/
3 opinion that no substantial question of law as proposed by appellants, arises in the present appeal.
17. No other arguments were advanced by counsel for appellants.

18. As no substantial question of law arises in the present appeal, accordingly, judgment and decree dated 21.10.2010 passed by District Judge, Vidisha in Regular Civil Appeal No. 24-A/2009, as well as judgment and decree dated 26.06.2009 passed by Civil Judge, Class I, Kurwai, District Vidisha in Civil Suit No. 37A/2008, are hereby affirmed.
19. Appeal fails and is hereby dismissed in limine.
